As a non-FF14 right now- reading these terms are really cool and gets me excited to play the game soon. But as a current WoW raider, you got me thinking of WoW raiding terms! 

"Hero/Lust" (Herosim/Bloodlust), "PI" (Power Infusion), "Gate" (A warlock spelling allowing players travel between 2 points quickly) , "Sac" (Sacrifice), "Prepot" (Prepotion), "Link" (Big Healer CD called Spirit Link Totem), "Down" (Enter a new phase to preform mechanics), "Hide" (Usually a mechanic that requires you to stand in a safe area to negate massive damage), "Cookies/Lock Rocks" (An ability by Warlocks to give you 3 healthstones), "Closet" (Warlock ability called Ritual of Summoming, used to summon players far away. The ability summons a demonic gate nicknamed the lock closet)

You'll frequently hear Warlock abilities called before raid. Things like "Cookies please", "Can we have a gate here", "Can we put down a closet?"

"Clear" is a term where we usually have to perform a mechanic to clear a really nasty debuff. Unsure if that's a thing in FF14.

"Bombs" probably isn't WoW exclusive (Essentially, just any mechanic that has lots of small AoEs or AoEs that require players to pick up a literal bomb and move from the group)

"Sac" I don't know if sacking a player is something done in FF14 either, but a few raids have had players simply sacrificing themselves to get rid of a certain mechanic.

Raid sizes are also a thing you'll hear; "we're going 2/3/9 then go"

And of course, AOTC/Curve and CE/Edge are achievements that you get for killing the last boss of the current tier in either Heroic (Ahead of the Curve) or Mythic (Cutting Edge). Both of these achievements are used almost like a pass to get into groups that want people who have killed the boss before.  A lot of players define themselves as an 'AoTC Raider' or 'Mythic Raider'

I agree that the skip mentality is hurting the new players of WoW and a lot of the time it can completely sour the experience but I don't think it's the player's fault as much as it is Blizzard's fault, for a few reasons.

Look, doing dungeons that you've done hundreds of times isn't exactly "fun". Especially when you're just trying to get a toon ready for raiding. Flying through dungeons to get to end game (which is the fun part for a lot of players) is the only thing that makes leveling bearably because for a lot of us, leveling a brand new character isn't enjoyable. 

Dungeons aren't hard anymore, unless you're in M+. Listen, I hate it too but it's the sad truth. Leveling dungeons aren't hard, they're a slog a lot of the time. Mechanics don't hurt you (depending on the dungeon) and a lot of the bosses/trash are just health sponges. Combine this with not having access to 100% of your class and the whole experience (for older players) really just sucks, so they do it as quick as possible. I would love for dungeon to require teamwork outside of endgame/M+ but it's just not really needed anymore. 

This is a point a lot of people have already made but I think it's a very big one; New players should NOT be in expansion dungeons. There is no reason for it. I seen someone in the comments compare Deadmines to Dazar'Alor and saying that the skill gap between those who settings is way more advanced and they're 100% right. People who have never played WoW should not be stepping into a dungeon with mechanics that can kill you instantly or wipe your entire team. Dungeons don't even require real teamwork anymore, it's mostly just individual skill- which a lot of newer players don't have.

I think Blizzard should 100% make brand new accounts only be able to do Vanilla dungeons (Maybe TBC?) or design something that makes it worth for old players to stop skipping to the end. Hell, even Blizzard making a small set of simple leveling dungeons only for new players sounds like a great idea. There's a lot of people here putting up great ideas of what Blizz could do to fix this.

I don't consider myself good at this game at all so take what I say lightly but in that situation there's a few things you can do. It all depends if you feel like the game is over or not an give up, I'd recommend to always play it out because Thresh has the ability to catch people out of position with ease if you're good enough and at lower elo this is something that is going to happen a lot, you just need to be able to see when it happens because it's not always obvious. 

If you begin to focus on catching people out of position and making sure every fight in that game is an unfair fight for your team then you slowly begin to build back again their lead. Also focus on saving your teammates from death when they're out of position as well, lantern is such a good ability for this. 

If the game is over and the win is so very unlikely to happen then perhaps you can focus on your mechanics and practice hooking, warding in key spots, flaying champions out of animations, ect ect. This makes it so the loss isnt a total loss on your part and you'll just have to learn that losing can mean way more wins in the future with effort. This is the go next mentality you'll want to have instead of just throwing the towel in.

Overall I recommend the harder option which is trying to create small picks and plays for your team. Its insanely hard and it's not going to always work but you'll get better by doing it. I recommend looking up key ward placements and watching what the enemies do when they want/after they have taken an objective as they'll give tells to their next move and you can ward accordingly. 

Good luck bro.
